scenes.tts: If you remove one receptor from a mouse, which neurons disappear, and when?
scenes.visual: Title card: Delete One, Count the Survivors. A mouse embryo with several ganglia outlined.
scenes.narration: If you remove one receptor from a mouse, which neurons disappear, and when?

scenes.tts: A knockout mouse is one in which a chosen gene has been disrupted.
scenes.visual: A gene on a chromosome is crossed out.
scenes.narration: A knockout mouse is one in which a chosen gene has been disrupted.

scenes.tts: It makes no working protein, or no working form of one protein.
scenes.visual: The receptor shape fades from the cell surface.
scenes.narration: It makes no working protein, or no working form of one protein.

scenes.tts: Delete each neurotrophin or Track gene, one at a time. The family sorts by which neurons are lost.
scenes.caption: Delete each neurotrophin or Trk gene, one at a time. The family sorts by which neurons are lost.
scenes.visual: A row of mice, each tagged with one missing gene.
scenes.narration: Delete each neurotrophin or Trk gene, one at a time. The family sorts by which neurons are lost.

scenes.tts: Start with Track A, and the sympathetic ganglion in the neck.
scenes.caption: Start with TrkA, and the sympathetic ganglion in the neck.
scenes.visual: Zoom to the superior cervical ganglion in a mouse lacking TrkA.
scenes.narration: Start with TrkA, and the sympathetic ganglion in the neck.

scenes.tts: Anne Fagan and colleagues counted its cells at several ages.
scenes.visual: An empty graph: cell count against age, wild type and TrkA-null lines. On screen: Fagan and colleagues, 1996.
scenes.narration: Anne Fagan and colleagues counted its cells at several ages.

scenes.tts: At embryonic day thirteen point five, the count was normal.
scenes.caption: At embryonic day 13.5, the count was normal.
scenes.visual: First points: at E13.5 the two lines start together.
scenes.narration: At embryonic day 13.5, the count was normal.

scenes.tts: If Track A is needed for survival, not for making the neurons, what should happen next?
scenes.caption: If TrkA is needed for survival, not for making the neurons, what should happen next?
scenes.visual: Graph pauses at E13.5. Question on screen: counts, divisions, deaths?
scenes.narration: If TrkA is needed for survival, not for making the neurons, what should happen next?

scenes.tts: The mutant fell steadily behind.
scenes.visual: The mutant line drops below the control. On screen: about 15% fewer at E15.5, 35% fewer at E17.5.
scenes.narration: The mutant fell steadily behind.

scenes.tts: At birth it had about half as many neurons as control ganglia.
scenes.visual: At birth the mutant point sits at about half. On screen: about 50% fewer.
scenes.narration: At birth it had about half as many neurons as control ganglia.

scenes.tts: By postnatal day nine, nearly all of its principal neurons were gone.
scenes.caption: By postnatal day 9, nearly all of its principal neurons were gone.
scenes.visual: At P9 the mutant line nears zero.
scenes.narration: By postnatal day 9, nearly all of its principal neurons were gone.

scenes.tts: Over those embryonic ages, dividing cells were no fewer than in controls. Dying cells, with shrunken nuclei, increased.
scenes.visual: Two insets labeled embryonic ages: mitotic figures, mutant bar level with control; pyknotic nuclei, mutant bar higher.
scenes.narration: Over those embryonic ages, dividing cells were no fewer than in controls. Dying cells, with shrunken nuclei, increased.

scenes.tts: So the neurons were made, and then they died.
scenes.visual: Label across the graph: made, then lost.
scenes.narration: So the neurons were made, and then they died.

scenes.tts: Now the other pairs. Mice lacking N G F or Track A lose sympathetic neurons.
scenes.caption: Now the other pairs. Mice lacking NGF or TrkA lose sympathetic neurons.
scenes.visual: A grid builds: genotype rows, neuron population columns. Row one: NGF or TrkA.
scenes.narration: Now the other pairs. Mice lacking NGF or TrkA lose sympathetic neurons.

scenes.tts: They also lose many small sensory neurons that sense pain and heat.
scenes.visual: Row one fills: sympathetic; small pain and heat neurons.
scenes.narration: They also lose many small sensory neurons that sense pain and heat.

scenes.tts: Mice lacking B D N F lose vestibular neurons, which sense balance and head movement.
scenes.caption: Mice lacking BDNF lose vestibular neurons, which sense balance and head movement.
scenes.visual: Row two, BDNF: vestibular neurons, with an inner-ear icon.
scenes.narration: Mice lacking BDNF lose vestibular neurons, which sense balance and head movement.

scenes.tts: They also lose many nodose petrosal neurons, which carry signals from the heart, lungs and gut.
scenes.caption: They also lose many nodose-petrosal neurons, which carry signals from the heart, lungs and gut.
scenes.visual: Row two adds nodose-petrosal neurons, with heart, lung and gut icons.
scenes.narration: They also lose many nodose-petrosal neurons, which carry signals from the heart, lungs and gut.

scenes.tts: Mice lacking N T four lose nodose petrosal neurons too.
scenes.caption: Mice lacking NT-4 lose nodose-petrosal neurons too.
scenes.visual: Row three, NT-4: nodose-petrosal neurons.
scenes.narration: Mice lacking NT-4 lose nodose-petrosal neurons too.

scenes.tts: And mice lacking N T three or Track C lose the sensory neurons that report where a limb is.
scenes.caption: And mice lacking NT-3 or TrkC lose the sensory neurons that report where a limb is.
scenes.visual: Row four, NT-3 or TrkC: proprioceptive afferents, with a limb icon.
scenes.narration: And mice lacking NT-3 or TrkC lose the sensory neurons that report where a limb is.

scenes.tts: These mice move and hold their limbs abnormally.
scenes.visual: A mouse with an awkward limb posture.
scenes.narration: These mice move and hold their limbs abnormally.

scenes.tts: In this grid, lose means fewer neurons. Usually part of a ganglion survives, but some groups are lost almost entirely.
scenes.visual: Note at the top of the grid: loses means fewer; usually partial, sometimes nearly all of a group.
scenes.narration: In this grid, lose means fewer neurons. Usually part of a ganglion survives, but some groups are lost almost entirely.

scenes.tts: Each pair has its own pattern of loss.
scenes.visual: The grid complete, each row a different color.
scenes.narration: Each pair has its own pattern of loss.

scenes.tts: But the map has overlaps. N T three prefers Track C, yet it also activates Track A and Track B.
scenes.caption: But the map has overlaps. NT-3 prefers TrkC, yet it also activates TrkA and TrkB.
scenes.visual: Dashed arrows from NT-3 to TrkA and TrkB.
scenes.narration: But the map has overlaps. NT-3 prefers TrkC, yet it also activates TrkA and TrkB.

scenes.tts: Should a mouse lacking N T three lose more neurons, or fewer, than one lacking Track C?
scenes.caption: Should a mouse lacking NT-3 lose more neurons, or fewer, than one lacking TrkC?
scenes.visual: Two mice side by side: no NT-3, no TrkC. Question on screen.
scenes.narration: Should a mouse lacking NT-3 lose more neurons, or fewer, than one lacking TrkC?

scenes.tts: Expect more. In many ganglia at the same age, mice lacking N T three lose more neurons than mice lacking Track C.
scenes.caption: Expect more. In many ganglia at the same age, mice lacking NT-3 lose more neurons than mice lacking TrkC.
scenes.visual: Two ganglion counts side by side, same age: no NT-3 lower than no TrkC.
scenes.narration: Expect more. In many ganglia at the same age, mice lacking NT-3 lose more neurons than mice lacking TrkC.

scenes.tts: That fits N T three also acting through Track A and Track B. The size of the gap depends on the ganglion and age.
scenes.caption: That fits NT-3 also acting through TrkA and TrkB. The size of the gap depends on the ganglion and age.
scenes.visual: A TrkC-null loss shape that largely lies inside the larger NT-3-null loss shape, with a note that the sets need not be exactly nested, labeled by ganglion and age.
scenes.narration: That fits NT-3 also acting through TrkA and TrkB. The size of the gap depends on the ganglion and age.

scenes.tts: Some populations also need more than one factor, at different stages.
scenes.visual: A timeline with two factors in sequence.
scenes.narration: Some populations also need more than one factor, at different stages.

scenes.tts: The takeaway: each factor and receptor pair has its own pattern of loss. In the sympathetic ganglion, neurons were made, then lost.
scenes.visual: Takeaway on screen: each factor-receptor pair has its own pattern of loss; in the TrkA-null sympathetic ganglion, made then lost.
scenes.narration: The takeaway: each factor and receptor pair has its own pattern of loss. In the sympathetic ganglion, neurons were made, then lost.
